headline: High risk: shared filesystem and broad write/network/MCP capabilities make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A reads/writes shared skill files and Agent B shares state via filesystem with MCP/browser inputs, so A’s content can reach B as untrusted instructions. The pathway is not proven by sandbox evidence, but both profiles expose a file-based bridge and B’s tool-use surface is permissive enough to be hijacked by attacker-controlled content.
conditions: IF Agent A writes instruction-like content into shared workspace files
IF Agent B ingests workspace files or MCP output without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic file ingestion in B
Add provenance tags to shared files
Review shared skill files before B reads them
requires-engineering: enforce content-signed handoff between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches marketing/product-marketing context and can write files; Agent B reads workspace files and has broad network egress plus model API calls. Shared filesystem state creates a plausible path for sensitive context to flow from A into B’s outputs or external API requests, though the exact data class is limited in the profiles.
conditions: IF sensitive marketing context is stored in the shared workspace
IF B sends workspace contents to its configured model API or MCP server
mitigations: Keep sensitive docs out of the shared workspace
Use separate API keys per agent
Turn off B access to shared files
Redact secrets before handoff
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on workspace reads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and support multiple instances; B also modifies git state and shares state via filesystem. That overlap creates a default conflict surface for clobbered files, race conditions, and git corruption, with no locking mechanism documented in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory
IF either agent writes git-tracked files while the other is active
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate repo clone
Pause one agent before the other writes
Avoid concurrent git operations
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add file and git locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate marketing content and shared skill files, while Agent B can treat workspace content as input and take downstream actions through shell, browser, or MCP tools. That makes A’s output a plausible upstream source for B’s actions without a documented verification step, so errors can cascade across work products.
conditions: IF B uses A-produced files as authoritative input
IF B executes shell or MCP actions based on unverified A output
mitigations: Require human review before B acts
Add a verification checklist between agents
Mark A outputs as draft-only
Restrict B to read-only mode for handoffs
requires-engineering: implement citation/provenance validation

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to the shared handling of marketing content and code. Because both profiles are docs-only and no regulated data class is named, the pairwise compliance concern is narrower than the other risks and does not justify a higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF retention or residency policies differ between the two operators
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention rules for shared files
Use separate storage locations
Review secrets handling before use
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls
